mathgap.title: Sequential processing of transfers
mathgap.principle: When a transfer statement appears, immediately adjust both the giver's and receiver's counts, subtracting from the giver and adding to the receiver, using the current counts at that point. This ensures later statements see the updated amounts.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence says 'X gives N items to Y' (or similar transfer wording).
mathgap.example: Only adding N to the receiver while leaving the giver unchanged.

mathgap.title: Signed difference equality
mathgap.principle: Translate statements that equate a signed difference to another difference as (A - B) = (C - D). Keep the order of terms to preserve sign information.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence says 'the number of X that has more than Y is equal to the difference between the number of A and B'.
mathgap.example: Treating the left side as |X - Y| instead of X - Y.

mathgap.title: Direct count assignment at point of mention
mathgap.principle: When a statement directly gives a count for a person (e.g., 'X has N items'), set that person's current count to N at that moment, overwriting any previous value. Subsequent statements refer to this new count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence provides an explicit count for a person.
mathgap.example: Treating the new count as a simultaneous constraint with earlier values, leading to contradictory equations.

mathgap.title: Non‑negative integer check
mathgap.principle: All item counts must be non‑negative integers; discard any solution that yields a negative or fractional count. This check should be applied after solving the system of equations.
mathgap.when_to_apply: After obtaining a candidate solution for all variables.
mathgap.example: Accepting a solution where a count is 275/9, which is fractional.

mathgap.title: Conditional transfer handling
mathgap.principle: For conditional transfers, first evaluate the condition using the current counts; only if the condition holds, transfer the specified amount (often all items) from the giver to the receiver.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence says 'If X has more than N items, X will transfer ...'.
mathgap.example: Transferring items regardless of whether the condition is satisfied.

mathgap.title: Redistribution equalization handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says two persons redistribute items to ensure each has an equal amount, pool their items and split the total evenly between them. Both persons receive the same final count.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence mentions 'X and Y redistribute ... to ensure each has an equal amount'.
mathgap.example: Adjusting only one person's count while leaving the other's unchanged.

mathgap.title: Multiplicative increase handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'the number of X increases by N times', multiply X's current count by N (i.e., X = X * N). This includes fractional multipliers, which should be applied exactly.
mathgap.when_to_apply: When a sentence uses the phrase 'increases by N times' (including fractional N).
mathgap.example: Adding N to X instead of multiplying, or rounding a fractional result.

mathgap.title: Directionality of more/fewer statements
mathgap.principle: Interpret 'X has N more than Y' as X - Y = N (i.e., X = Y + N) and 'X has N fewer than Y' as X - Y = -N. Preserve the order of the names to keep the sign correct.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence uses 'more' or 'fewer' to compare counts.
mathgap.example: Reversing the direction and writing Y - X = N.

mathgap.title: Swap handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X and Y switch the items they have', exchange the counts of X and Y. No other changes occur.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence uses the word 'switch' to describe two persons swapping their items.
mathgap.example: Leaving both counts unchanged or adding them together instead of swapping.

mathgap.title: Split-all handling
mathgap.principle: When a statement says 'X splits all the items she owns equally among Y and Z', give each of Y and Z half of X's original amount; X ends with zero unless X is one of the recipients, in which case X retains half.
mathgap.when_to_apply: Whenever a sentence uses 'splits all the ... equally among' phrasing.
mathgap.example: Assuming X always ends with zero, even when X is listed as a recipient.

mathgap.description: Treating signed difference statements as absolute differences
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model defaults to interpreting 'difference' as a magnitude, ignoring the order of terms.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Always keep the order of the names; treat 'X - Y' as a signed quantity, not |X - Y|.

mathgap.description: Ignoring the sequential order of transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model treats all transfer statements as independent constraints rather than a time‑ordered process.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Process statements in the exact order given, updating counts after each transfer before evaluating the next statement.

mathgap.description: Assuming explicit counts are final after all transfers
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model interprets each count sentence as a permanent equation that must hold alongside earlier values.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: When a direct count appears, overwrite the person's current count with the given number; earlier values are discarded for that person.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting 'increase by N times' as addition rather than multiplication
mathgap.why_it_happens: The word 'times' is confused with 'more', leading the model to add instead of multiply.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: Apply exact multiplication: new count = old count * N, even when N is fractional.

mathgap.description: Misinterpreting split-all statements as leaving the original person with zero even when they are a recipient
mathgap.why_it_happens: Model applies a generic split rule without checking whether the splitter appears among the recipients.
mathgap.how_to_avoid: If the splitter is listed as one of the recipients, give them half of the original amount and the other recipient the other half; otherwise the splitter ends with zero.
